reviewText: Different enough to avoid becoming ridiculous, but not original enough to truly excite, Taken 3 may satisfy action fans but it's unlikely anybody will be begging for part four.

The storytelling's a bit unmoored, but Paul Rudd shines in a colorful cantina of weird alien creatures and Jonathan Majors gives a charismatic pathos to Kang the Conqueror. Isn't it nice to have MCU movies that are just plain fun again?
With his third kidnapping caper, Taken 3, Liam Neeson takes self-parody to new lows and the result is hysterically, enjoyably bad.
Taken 3 isn't a good movie. Against all logic, it isn't a bad movie, either. Instead, it's so casual and indifferent to itself it lapses into something altogether appalling.
The movie stinks. It doesn't stink in a clever or interesting way. It's not even so bad that it's funny.
There are some big ideas here, and the attempts at world-building are ambitiously borrowed, but much the same as its unlikely Avenger, Quantumania comes up small.
Let's face facts...we all were Taken in by this pseudo punchy action yarn that no longer generates the destructive heat it once punctuated with carefree confidence.
Limping toward the film's climax with a bizarre underwear fight might have sealed it.
Flailing handheld camerawork, frantic over-editing and claustrophobic close-ups make it basically impossible to distinguish Mills from his enemies, or to decipher the geography of a given scene.
Neeson's late-life rebirth as an action star may be drawing to a close with this limping, wheezing entry in the "Taken" franchise.

It's not actively awful in any kind of meaningful way, because it's not remarkable enough to be that. Instead, it's a filler episode in the TV-ification of the MCU. It's fine if you miss it, because the next episode / movie will catch you up on it.

Ant-Man and The Wasp: Quantumania may be lacking in any discernible drama or emotional stakes but it is easily one of the most solidly entertaining and spectacular of Marvel’s ‘Phase 4’ run of of film and TV.
Marvel’s mini-hero is back in a movie that’s all scale, no fun.
Please don't bother with Taken 3. There's nothing redeemable about it.
The Taken series is a right-wing male revenge fantasy and while we write these films off as silly and puerile they're influencing how Americans are seeing the world.
Kang remains more myth than menace and, save for a few dorky gags and sweet father-daughter moments, it's an easily missable movie.
Is it worth watching this to keep up with the MCU? Sure. It's hard not to root for the "little guy." But this movie is "just fine" instead of particularly funny, thrilling, or memorable.
Taken 3 may be this movie's title, but the only thing taken here will be your money if you decide to pay to see what is the worst film in this franchise.
Does Kang bang? Why yes, he does. Majors brings the same emotionally intense it-boy energy of Adam Driver in The Force Awakens.

Quantumania maintains the quirky fun of the Ant-Man movies and is a great introduction to Kang but it struggles with massively combating tones. It's solid entertainment but the MCU bag of tricks have become redundant and exhausting.
​I'll tell you what got "Taken." A hundred and twelve minutes of my life got "Taken."

Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania, a film that blasts into a galaxy far, far away. While there are plenty of bumps on the journey, it's hard not to be fully invested in Jonathan Majors' magnetic presence and Paul Rudd's contagious charm.
Quantumania swings big, but forgets the small stuff, to its own detriment.

Quantumania triumphs in its presentation of the new villain of the saga. Not only is Kang's character menacing, but his motivations and characteristics are resolved with grace.  [Full review in Spanish]
'Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania' is the weirdest, most fun movie of the three. Yet, it's bogged down by serving as another stepping stone on the road to Marvel's Multiverse Saga.
And yet, there it was, that thought, overarching and overwhelming: “I didn’t feel a thing.”
How is something that is supposed to be small become something that is way, way, way too much?
[A] blockbuster that’s never compelling for more than five minutes at a time and has nothing original or special to contribute to the superhero genre.
It's the weakest of the trilogy, but Taken 3 kicks just hard enough to survive another day.
the charismatic presence of Liam Neeson and his impenetrable sense of decency carry the film way beyond its thrilling action sequences.
Thriller fans looking for a bit of brainless biff will lap it up.
No one gets taken. That's my beef. No one. Gets. Taken. I mean, come on.
